parameters.note: The meal slot a new meal starts on, from the phone's clock (K-407): an active, low-cost entry is pre-filled (I2 G1, layer A), and the slot is one tap to change. Each slot runs from its hour to the next one's; before the first hour it is the last slot (a late snack).
FoodSearch.q minLength: a shorter search is refused by the server, so the phone does not send it.

Search as you type (ADR-085 #1): how long the box waits after the last key before it asks the server. Short enough that the list follows the typing, long enough that a word being typed is one request, not one per letter. The keyboard's Search key does not wait.

A serving named by one of these is a volume measure (ADR-085 #5): a food is not opened on it by default, because a cup of dried egg or of flour says little about what was eaten. Whole words in any case or plural; the first serving that has none of them, or grams, is the default unit.
The amount a food opens on when it is counted in grams (ADR-085 #5): 100 g, the basis the database's values are given in, so the estimate shows at once and the user changes it. A serving opens on 1.
FoodSearch.q maxLength.
FoodSearch.limit: the contract's default, sent as it is (the generated type asks for it). Best matches come first; a longer list is scrolled past, not read.
Amount: the amount an item makes is at most 5000 g; a larger one would be refused by the server and the meal lost from the queue.
Amount.quantity: at most 2 decimals.
FoodEstimateRequest.items maxItems; the server checks a logged meal's items the same way (K-407 review: a larger meal was queued, refused and lost).
One tap of - or + on a food counted in grams (the one Stepper, ADR-070 Ek 2 #5; K-1046). The amount opens on meal_default_grams (100 g), so ten is a tenth of it; any other amount is typed.

One tap of - or + on a food counted in servings or on a recipe's portions (the one Stepper, ADR-070 Ek 2 #5; K-1046). Half a serving is the smallest part people say ("half a bowl"); any other amount is typed, up to Amount.quantity's 2 decimals.
The amount field's length: room for the largest amount the contract takes with its 2 decimals (5000.00), and a little more for typing.
BarcodeLookup.gtin pattern ^[0-9]{8,14}$: EAN-8 and UPC-E have 8 digits (a UPC-E is expanded by the server, K-208).
GTIN-14, the longest the contract takes.
The typed barcode field's length: the longest GTIN (14 digits) and a little room for stray spaces, which are trimmed.
A recipe's name, trimmed, in code points (NewRecipe.name, ADR-034): the phone stops at the server's limit.
How many portions a recipe can make (NewRecipe.portions, 1..50, a whole number).
A meal photo leaves the phone at most this long a side (anayasa V1: image cost -74%). The server refuses a longer one (keel.coach.photo.max-side, ADR-046) rather than shrink it.
The JPEG the phone writes from the shrunk photo (K-408, ADR-046): small enough to send quickly, clear enough to tell the foods apart. The server writes its own again (0.85).

How many of the foods eaten lately (GET /v1/foods/recent, K-1025) the meal screen lists for one tap (K-980): twelve since K-1063 (ADR-090 Ek 3: two was too few to be a shortcut). The server orders them (the slot's own first, then the freshest) and sends up to keel.nutrition.recent-foods (application.yml, 12); this is how many of those the screen shows, so it is never more than the server's ceiling (backend NutritionLimitsTests mirrors it).

The hour a meal logged into a day that is not today is given (the app has no clock to read for it, and a day's order is by time): the usual hour of the slot. Today's meals take the moment they are logged.
How many days back the Food page's day strip goes (ADR-090 Ek 3: at least a month of logged days can be read, changed and logged into).
How far back "Log again" looks for a meal to log once more (one tap).
How many past meals "Log again" lists, the freshest first, one of each kind of meal.

The meal slots offered are the ones the user logged into in this many days (and today's); a user with fewer than two such slots sees all four. One tap adds the others (ADR-090 Ek 3: "I eat N meals a day").
The quantities a portion offers as one-tap chips beside the stepper, for a food counted in pieces or servings ("half", 1, 2, 3): the common cases need no typing.
One tap of - or + on a food counted in ounces (the grams' step, 10 g, is about a third of an ounce; half an ounce is the smallest part a US scale shows).
Contract QuickEntry.kcal: a quick add is at most this (a day's worth of food at most).
Contract QuickEntry: protein, carbs and fat of a quick add are at most this many grams each.
Contract NewFood.name: the longest name of a food the user adds from a label.
The serving size an own food starts on (a label's own: 100 g, the basis most labels also give); the user changes it to the label's.

How far a logged item is swiped to the left to delete it (iOS list habit: a short swipe shows the red Delete, a long one does it). Past it the item goes and the app's banner offers Undo; short of it the row springs back. Product choice, no source gives a distance.

The small hint under the day's numbers (about 600 kcal a meal) is the day's target over the meal slots the user uses, rounded to this: a guide to the size of a meal, not a budget per meal (U7). Rounded so it does not read as a precise rule.

The per-meal hint ("2 meals a day, about 1,200 kcal each") is shown only once the user's own pattern exists: meals logged on at least this many different days within slots_used_window_days. On the first day the slots are a guess from one or two meals, and the hint would present that guess as the user's habit (K-1066).

The meal the screen opens on follows the user's own pattern once a meal has this many logs in the window (slots_used_window_days): the slot whose usual time of day is nearest to now. Fewer, and the clock decides (meal_slot_starts).

The user's pattern picks a meal only when its usual time is within this many minutes of now; further away, the clock decides. A product choice (two and a half hours is about the gap between a usual breakfast and lunch).
How many favorites the empty search shows before 'Show all' (the list stays one screen, not a library).
How many of the foods usually had at this meal the empty search shows.
How many recent foods the empty search shows before 'Show more' (quick_recent_max is the most it shows then).
How many whole past meals of the slot are offered as one row each ('Same as yesterday's breakfast').
How many of the meal's items the tray shows as chips before the rest are one '+N' chip that opens the day.
How long a row that was just logged shows its check instead of the plus.

A logged item swiped left this far of the Delete button's width stays open with the red Delete showing (a tap on it deletes); less springs back. The iOS list habit: a swipe shows the button, it does not delete by itself.
A logged item swiped left this far across its row is deleted with the swipe (iOS Mail's full swipe); the app's banner offers Undo. Between the two thresholds the button is shown and waits for a tap.
